title: College Football Week 8 Live Updates: USC, Kentucky, Clemson Scores & Schedule on CBS Sports
body:
The college football landscape shifted dramatically on Saturday as the Week 8 slate unfolded, featuring marquee matchups that could reshape conference races and bowl aspirations. The University of Southern California trod onto the field against a resilient Washington State squad, Kentucky clashed with a surging Florida State team, and Clemson faced a gritty Georgia Tech side—all while the nation watched a cascade of upsets that had already toppled five of the top‑seven teams the week before. The results left fans buzzing, coaches recalibrating, and the playoff picture looking more fluid than ever in what many are calling one of the most unpredictable seasons in recent memory.

USC entered the contest riding a three‑game winning streak and hoping to solidify its place among the Pac‑12’s elite. The Trojans’ high‑octane offense, anchored by sophomore quarterback Michael Penix Jr., exploded for 42 points, but Washington State’s relentless defense kept the game within reach until the final drive. A late‑game interception returned for a touchdown sealed a 38‑31 victory for the Trojans, propelling them to the top of the Pac‑12 West and giving them a crucial boost in the College Football Playoff (CFP) rankings. Penix’s poise under pressure, highlighted by a 320‑yard passing performance and three touchdowns, reaffirmed his status as a contender for the Heisman race, while the Cougars’ defensive coordinator, Alex Grinch, earned praise for a scheme that forced the Trojans into uncomfortable third‑down situations.

Across the country in Lexington, Kentucky’s Wildcats sought to bounce back from a humbling loss to Arkansas. Their opponent, Florida State, arrived with momentum after a decisive win over Louisville. The Seminoles’ balanced attack—combining a potent rushing game led by freshman running back Jordan Travis with a deep‑passing threat in quarterback Jordan Travis (yes, the same name) — proved too much for the Wildcats. Kentucky’s defense struggled to contain the Seminoles’ tempo, resulting in a 45‑24 defeat that dropped the Wildcats out of the top‑25. Florida State, meanwhile, vaulted into the top‑15, positioning itself as a dark horse for the ACC championship. The game also highlighted the growing impact of transfer players, as Florida State’s veteran linebacker, former Ohio State standout J.T. Tuimoloau, recorded a career‑high 12 tackles and two sacks, underscoring the evolving dynamics of roster building in the modern era.

In the ACC’s Atlantic Division, Clemson faced a familiar foe in Georgia Tech, a matchup that carried both historical weight and immediate implications for the Tigers’ quest to reclaim conference supremacy. The Tigers, still reeling from a shocking loss to Miami the previous week, leaned heavily on senior quarterback DJ Uiagalelei, whose poise in the pocket was evident as he amassed 285 yards and two touchdowns. However, Georgia Tech’s disciplined defense forced three turnovers, including a crucial fumble recovered in the red zone that halted a Clemson drive late in the third quarter. The game concluded with a 31‑27 win for the Tigers, a narrow margin that kept them within striking distance of the ACC title but also exposed lingering vulnerabilities in their secondary. Defensive coordinator Brent Venables’ decision to rotate additional nickel packages paid dividends, yet the need for a more consistent pass rush remains a talking point among analysts.

The Week 8 outcomes reverberated beyond the individual contests, amplifying the narrative of a season defined by volatility. With five top‑seven teams having fallen in Week 7, the CFP committee now faces a more complex calculus, as each victory or loss carries amplified weight. Teams like USC and Florida State, which entered the week with solid but not spectacular rankings, now find themselves in contention for the coveted top‑four spots, while traditional powerhouses such as Alabama and Ohio State, both of whom posted comfortable wins, must guard against complacency. The ripple effect also extends to recruiting battles; high‑school prospects are closely monitoring how programs respond to adversity, and early‑season performance often influences their final commitments.

Looking ahead, the next two weeks promise to further test the mettle of the season’s frontrunners. USC’s upcoming clash with Oregon will serve as a litmus test for the Trojans’ ability to maintain momentum against a formidable Pac‑12 opponent, while Kentucky must regroup quickly if they hope to salvage a respectable conference finish. Clemson’s schedule features a pivotal showdown with Notre Dame, a game that could either cement the Tigers’ resurgence or expose deeper systemic issues. As the drama intensifies, fans and analysts alike will be watching not just for scores, but for the emerging storylines that could define the 2026 college football year—whether it be a surprise breakout team, a late‑season rally, or the continued erosion of the traditional power hierarchy.
